## Setting up the physical system

A 5 MWh**th** molten‑salt store (think: small two‑tank "solar salt" unit, NaNO₃/KNO₃, not a battery) is defined by:

- **Energy density of the salt swing**: ρ·cₚ·ΔT. Solar salt: ρ≈1,800 kg/m³, cₚ≈1.5 kJ/kg·K. A modest ΔT between cold and hot tank of ~250°C (vs. ~290°C used at utility CSP scale) gives ≈675 MJ/m³ ≈ **190 kWh_th/m³**.
- For 5,000 kWh of capacity: **~27 m³ of salt**, call it ~30 m³ with ullage → **~54 tonnes of salt**.

## Bottom-up cost buildup

| Component | Basis | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Salt (54 t @ ~$700–750/t, small-lot price) | | ~$40k |
| Hot tank (316-class stainless, ~565°C service, insulated, elevated/cooled foundation) | | ~$120k |
| Cold tank (carbon steel, ~290°C) | | ~$60k |
| Insulation (tanks + piping) | | ~$40k |
| Two high-temp molten-salt pumps (vertical cantilever, custom — no mass-market equivalent) | | ~$80k |
| Salt/steam or salt/oil heat exchanger | | ~$150k |
| High-temp piping, valves, electric trace heating (freeze protection) | | ~$90k |
| Instrumentation, controls, electrical BOP | | ~$50k |
| **Equipment subtotal** | | **~$630k** |
| Installation/construction (~40% of equipment) | | ~$250k |
| Engineering/EPC/PM (~15%) | | ~$95k |
| Contingency (~12%) | | ~$115k |
| **Total installed** | | **~$1.09M** |

**→ ~$220/kWh installed**, for a 5 MWh system.

**Cross-check via scaling law:** utility-scale CSP molten-salt TES (hundreds-of-MWh systems) runs ~$20–25/kWh (NREL/SAM figures). Capital-equipment costs scale roughly with the "six-tenths rule," cost ∝ capacity^0.6–0.7 at this size range (pumps, HX, and controls have a large fixed-cost floor that doesn't shrink proportionally). Scaling a $22/kWh, 1,000 MWh reference down to 5 MWh with exponent 0.6 gives **~$180/kWh**; with exponent 0.5 (more fixed-cost-dominated, realistic at this small scale), **~$310/kWh**. My bottom-up $220/kWh sits right in that band — good consistency. The key insight: **5 MWh is small enough that molten-salt TES loses most of the scale economy that makes it look cheap in CSP literature.**

## Levelized cost of delivered heat

- Life: 25 yr (tank/pump mechanical life, not a chemical degradation limit), discount rate 7% → CRF ≈ 0.086
- Annualized capital: $1.09M × 0.086 ≈ **$94k/yr**
- O&M (trace-heat power, pump maintenance, inspection) ≈ 2%/yr ≈ **$22k/yr**
- Round-trip efficiency: small tanks have a worse surface/volume ratio than utility tanks, so standby+cycling losses are higher — assume **~85%** (vs. ~98–99% for huge CSP tanks)
- Duty: ~300 full cycles/yr → delivered energy = 5,000 kWh × 0.85 × 300 ≈ 1,275 MWh/yr

**LCOS ≈ $116k / 1,275,000 kWh ≈ 9¢/kWh of heat delivered.**

## Li-ion comparison (same 5 MWh, same duty)

- Installed cost: containerized LFP at this scale (small enough that it's 1–2 standard containers, so it mostly dodges the small-plant penalty) runs **~$350–450/kWh** in 2025–26 → **~$2.0M** total
- Life: 15 yr (calendar-life limited, well within cycle-life rating), CRF@7% ≈ 0.11 → annualized capital ≈ **$220k/yr**; O&M ~2% ≈ **$40k/yr**
- RTE ≈ 92%, same 300 cycles/yr → 1,380 MWh/yr delivered **as electricity**

**LCOS ≈ $260k / 1,380,000 kWh ≈ 19¢/kWh of electricity delivered.**

## Is molten salt competitive? — depends what you need out the other end

- **If the output is heat** (industrial process heat, "electric thermal storage" charged resistively): molten salt wins clearly, ~9¢/kWh vs. Li-ion+resistor's ~19¢/kWh — roughly **half the cost**, even at this unfavorable small scale.
- **If the output is electricity**: you must add a turbine-generator to convert the heat back, which (a) costs more than the storage itself at 5 MWh scale, and (b) caps round-trip efficiency at ~35–40% (steam cycle) unless you build an elaborate Carnot-battery heat pump arrangement. Once that's priced in, molten-salt-to-electricity is **not competitive** with Li-ion at this scale — it only wins at utility CSP scale (hundreds of MWh+) where the power block is shared infrastructure already being built for other reasons.
- The 5 MWh scale itself matters: it's a bad size for molten salt (every component is custom-fabricated, well below the minimum efficient scale for pumps/HX/engineering) but roughly scale-neutral for Li-ion (modular, mass-produced containers). A fairer fight for molten salt would be at 500+ MWh.

**Bottom line:** ~$220/kWh installed capital cost, ~9¢/kWh levelized for heat delivered. Cost-competitive with (actually cheaper than) Li-ion *for heat*, but not for electricity at this small scale without a disproportionately expensive power-conversion island.
